checks.comparison: Source Algorithm 1: w^{k+1} = w_base - gamma grad f(w_grad; eta), eta ~ D_xi, edge weighted by that gradient; reuse of an earlier computed gradient as in the Local SGD example (line 320). Elaborated Hist.step T gamma k h reply sets node k+1 := nodes(base k) - gamma * (if grad k = k then reply else replies(grad k)) and records reply as call k; birch queries nodes(point count) each step (one oracle call per step) and applies Hist.step; realize does the same with g(nodes(point k))(eta k).

Source Definition 2.1 (line 340): path from x^0 = w^0 with x^{k+1} a direct successor of x^k; (z^k, xi^k) generating the edge. Elaborated IsMainBranch T m := m 0 = 0 /\ forall k, 0 < m(k+1) /\ base(m(k+1) - 1) = m k; auxSample T m k := grad(m(k+1) - 1) (the call whose reply weights the edge into x^{k+1}); auxNode := point(auxSample) (the point where that gradient was evaluated, i.e. z^k).

Source Definition 2.2: max number of edges to the closest common ancestor (lines 409-411). Elaborated depth = fold 0 (+1); ancestors j = fold {0} (insert (k+1)) (the root path of j including j); dist T y z = max(depth y - sup_{a in anc y ∩ anc z} depth a, depth z - same).

Source Definition 2.3 (lines 414-416): multiset of stochastic gradients applied to w^0 to reach y. Elaborated repr T j = fold 0 (fun k M => grad k ::m M) j: the multiset of call indices weighting the edges of j's root path.

Source: minimise f : R^d -> R accessed only through stochastic gradients grad f(x;xi), xi ~ D_xi (lines 132-148). Elaborated gradientOracle {d}{Omega}[MeasurableSpace Omega] (P : ProbabilityMeasure (N -> Omega)) (g : Point d -> Omega -> Point d) : Oracle (Point d) (Point d) answers a query q with g q.2 seed, one Omega-valued tape entry per call; Point d is the Euclidean space PiLp 2 (Fin d -> R) (from the gradient/norm instances in the records).
Source: E||grad f(xbar)||^2 <= eps (line 138). EpsStationary f x P eps := Integrable (fun w => ||gradient f (x w)||^2) P /\ integral of ||gradient f (x w)||^2 dP <= eps (elaborated value).

Source: the run is a weighted directed tree G=(V,E) rooted at w^0 (line 318). Elaborated Tree is a structure of base/point/grad : N -> N (fields visible as providers Tree.base/point/grad); WellFormed T := forall j, base j <= j /\ point j <= j /\ grad j <= j; foldHist/fold recurse over the creation steps so node k+1 is computed from its parent base k.

base k / point k play w_base / w_grad, and grad k selects the fresh reply (grad k = k) or an earlier stored reply (the accepted reuse interpretation). Every step still evaluates one stochastic gradient at point k, matching 'compute a stochastic gradient at w_grad'; when grad k != k that evaluation is unused, which is the source of the 2-calls-per-iteration accounting accepted at plan stage. The tree is fixed data (accepted interpretation).
m(k+1) is created by step m(k+1)-1 whose parent is m k, so x^{k+1} is a direct child of x^k; xi^k is identified by its call index (the tape sample), z^k by the evaluation point. Faithful.

Common ancestors lie on a chain from the root, so the maximal depth among them is the closest common ancestor's depth; the natural subtraction is nonnegative there. Matches max{edges from y, edges from z}.
A call index determines both point (point c) and sample (tape c), so this is the source multiset of (point, sample) pairs; reused gradients appear with multiplicity as in the source.

The oracle returns exactly g(x, xi) at the queried point, nothing else (no function values, no exact gradients); the tape law P on N -> Omega is the place where sample laws/independence are imposed by the setups. No extra assumption is introduced here.
Exactly the squared-norm convention (eps not squared); the integrability conjunct only makes the source expectation meaningful. P is an explicit measure argument.
Node j+1's unique parent is base j <= j and gradients/reused replies refer only to already computed nodes/calls, exactly the source construction. Nothing added.
Definitions are total; domain restrictions (WellFormed, positivity) are left to the setups, as planned. gamma is any real (source: gamma >= 0), constrained by consumers.
auxNode/auxSample bind z^k, xi^k to the main branch m consistently with IsMainBranch (both use m(k+1)-1).
IsMainBranch is a conjunction m0 = 0 and forall k (child condition), correct polarity.
No assumptions are hidden in these definitions; the oracle law and A1-A3 are imposed elsewhere.
stepSize/horizon expressions equal Theorem 2.4's formulas with the R=0, sigma=0 conventions.
Initialisation x0, update order (count-indexed), one query per step, output node branch(seed) with seed uniform on Fin(K+1): the template executor for any Birch tree.

Seed law uniform PMF; oracle tape law an arbitrary ProbabilityMeasure on N -> Omega; their joint law is fixed by the template (product), consistent with the source independence of the output index from the samples.
Accuracy notion only; convergence statements belong to other units.
Gradients identified by call index; repr as Multiset N, multiplicities preserved.
Providers are Mathlib/template constants (Algorithm, Oracle, PMF.uniformOfFintype, gradient, integral, Finset, Multiset) and Rennala.Point; no project-local unreviewed provider affects meaning.
Unit declarations equal the inventory (23 declarations), all in module LongTails.Algorithms.BirchSgd, no dependencies on other run units.
R = 0 and sigma = 0 branches in stepSize; natural subtraction in dist is applied to depths that are >= the common-ancestor depth; K = 0 gives a one-point seed space.
